Courageous

kuh-RAY-jus — contains 'courage'; a courageous act comes straight from the heart. · adjective

Hear It

What It Means

Courageous is not deterred by danger or pain; brave.

The courageous whistleblower risked her entire career to expose the company's illegal dumping.

Worked Example

A ten-year-old sees a much older classmate being teased by a whole group of kids and, despite being frightened of the group's size, walks right over and stands beside the classmate until the teasing stops.

Facing something frightening head-on because it's the right thing to do is exactly what courageous means. Unlike 'reckless,' which ignores real danger foolishly, courageous means acting bravely despite recognizing the risk.

How Courageous Sits Among Its Neighbors

Synonyms — open each to see how it differs

brave

brave: willing to face danger or pain

valiant

valiant: showing great courage, especially in a difficult situation

fearless

fearless: showing no fear

Antonyms

cowardly

cowardly: lacking courage; too afraid to act

timid

timid: showing a lack of courage or confidence

How Strong Is It? — bold → courageous → heroic

bold vs. courageous

bold vs. courageous: Bold is a milder word than courageous — being bold means being confident and willing to take a risk, while courageous specifically means facing real danger or pain without backing down.

heroic vs. courageous

heroic vs. courageous: Heroic can feel bigger than courageous: courageous describes real bravery, but heroic adds the sense that the brave act actually saved someone or made a real difference.

Build the Word

The pieces

root — cour-

root — cour-: heart (Latin cor, 'heart', via Old French corage)

suffix — -age

suffix — -age: state or quality of (Old French, from Latin -aticum)

suffix — -ous

suffix — -ous: full of, possessing (Latin)

Put it together

Put it together: Latin cor meant 'heart' -- spelled cour- in English. Old French added -age to make corage ('heart, spirit'), and -ous ('full of') completes courageous: being completely full of heart -- facing fear with real inner strength.
